content.text:
I've read the release and the brief line by line. Here's my check.

**Key facts:** all ten are present and correctly stated — figures, periods and GAAP/non-GAAP basis all line up with the release tables. Notably the brief correctly flags the ~$8,700M free cash flow as *second-quarter year-to-date and estimated*, rather than passing it off as a quarterly actual, and it consistently labels operational/adjusted figures as non-GAAP.

**Claims:** I split the brief into 31 atomic assertions. Every one checks out against the release. A few notes on the judgment calls:

- The absence claims in "Capital and balance sheet" (no balance sheet, debt, dividend or repurchase detail) are verifiable by inspection of the release text and are accurate; the release's own list of accompanying schedules names only supplementary sales data, a condensed statement of earnings, non-GAAP reconciliations and key product sales.
- "The forward-looking statements cite the planned separation of the Orthopaedics business and the inability to predict legal outcomes" — both elements are in the release, though the legal-outcome language actually sits in the guidance paragraph rather than the forward-looking-statements note. The substance is right, so I passed it; the attribution is slightly loose.
- Watch-item bullets are mostly questions for management, which I skipped, except where they restate a fact (the ~760bp STELARA impact, and reported EPS falling while adjusted EPS rose).

No arithmetic the release doesn't show is relied on anywhere — the guidance raise amounts ($0.13, $0.18) and the 7.3% midpoint growth are all printed in the release rather than derived.

facts.evidence: Reported Q2 sales were $25,310 million versus $23,743 million, up 6.6%.
reported diluted EPS was $2.27 versus $2.29 (-0.9%)
adjusted diluted EPS (non-GAAP) was $2.90 versus $2.77, up 4.7%
Innovative Medicine sales were $16,384 million, +7.8% reported and +6.8% operational (non-GAAP), with divestitures a 10 basis point drag.
Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance (non-GAAP) was raised $0.13 to a $11.68 midpoint (range $11.60–$11.75)
Full-year 2026 estimated reported sales guidance is $100.8B–$101.4B, midpoint $101.1B (7.3% growth at midpoint), raised from $100.3B–$101.3B in April 2026.

Free cash flow (non-GAAP) was approximately $8,700 million, which the release footnotes as second-quarter year-to-date 2026 and estimated as of July 15, 2026, against $6,214 million in the prior-year column.
MedTech sales were $8,926 million, +4.5% reported and +3.6% operational (non-GAAP), with net acquisitions and divestitures a 10 basis point drag.

Operational sales growth (non-GAAP, excluding translational currency) was 5.6%, and adjusted operational sales growth (non-GAAP, excluding net acquisitions/divestitures and translational currency) was 5.7%.
Offsets were STELARA — an approximate 760 basis point impact — plus REMICADE, IMBRUVICA and ZYTIGA.

claims.claim: Johnson & Johnson reported 6.6% Q2 2026 sales growth to $25.3 billion.
Johnson & Johnson raised full-year 2026 sales and adjusted EPS guidance.
Reported net earnings and diluted EPS were essentially flat to slightly lower year over year.
Reported Q2 sales were $25,310 million versus $23,743 million a year earlier, up 6.6%.
Operational sales growth (non-GAAP, excluding translational currency) was 5.6%.
Adjusted operational sales growth (non-GAAP, excluding net acquisitions/divestitures and translational currency) was 5.7%.
Currency contributed 1.0 point to worldwide sales growth.
Reported net earnings were $5,534 million versus $5,537 million, a 0.1% decline.
Reported diluted EPS was $2.27 versus $2.29, a 0.9% decline.
Adjusted net earnings (non-GAAP, excluding intangible amortization and special items) were $7,081 million versus $6,699 million, up 5.7%.
Adjusted diluted EPS (non-GAAP) was $2.90 versus $2.77, up 4.7%.
Free cash flow (non-GAAP) was approximately $8,700 million, footnoted as second-quarter year-to-date 2026 and estimated as of July 15, 2026, against $6,214 million in the prior-year column.
U.S. sales were $14,533 million, up 7.3% reported and 7.3% operational (non-GAAP).
International sales were $10,777 million, up 5.7% reported and 3.4% operational (non-GAAP), with 2.3 points of currency.
Innovative Medicine sales were $16,384 million, up 7.8% reported and 6.8% operational (non-GAAP).
Divestitures were a 10 basis point drag on Innovative Medicine operational growth.
Innovative Medicine growth drivers cited were DARZALEX, CARVYKTI, TECVAYLI and RYBREVANT/LAZCLUZE in Oncology; TREMFYA and Other Immunology; SPRAVATO and CAPLYTA in Neuroscience.
Offsets to Innovative Medicine growth were STELARA (an approximate 760 basis point impact), REMICADE, IMBRUVICA and ZYTIGA.
MedTech sales were $8,926 million, up 4.5% reported and 3.6% operational (non-GAAP).
Net acquisitions and divestitures were a 10 basis point drag on MedTech operational growth.
MedTech growth drivers were wound closure and biosurgery in Surgery; electrophysiology and Shockwave in Cardiovascular; contact lenses in Vision; trauma in Orthopaedics.
Full-year 2026 estimated reported sales guidance is $100.8B–$101.4B with a midpoint of $101.1B, representing 7.3% growth at the midpoint.
The reported sales guidance was raised from an April 2026 range of $100.3B–$101.3B.
Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance (non-GAAP) was raised by $0.13 to a midpoint of $11.68, with a range of $11.60–$11.75.
Full-year 2026 adjusted operational EPS guidance (non-GAAP) was raised by $0.18 to a midpoint of $11.58.
The company states it does not provide forward-looking GAAP measures, citing inability to predict legal proceedings and other items.
The reported-sales guidance uses an illustrative Euro average rate of $1.15, versus $1.17 in April 2026.
The release discloses free cash flow (non-GAAP) only and provides no balance sheet, debt, dividend or share repurchase detail.
The release notes that cash flow from operations, the comparable GAAP measure, will be included in subsequent SEC filings.
Announced capital deployment includes more than $1 billion invested in U.S. Vision manufacturing in Jacksonville, Florida.
Announced capital deployment includes an agreement to acquire Firefly Bio.
Announced capital deployment includes a DePuy Synthes agreement to acquire miniature radiofrequency tracking technology.
Reported EPS fell while adjusted EPS rose.
The difference between reported EPS of $2.27 and adjusted EPS of $2.90 consists of intangible amortization expense and special items.
The release's forward-looking statements reference the planned separation of the Orthopaedics business and the inability to predict legal outcomes.
The release contains a talc disclosure reference.
